title: How injured Tejaswin put aside heartbreak to help Kushare script CWG history
content: Tejaswin Shankar's Commonwealth Games high jump ended due to injury. He then coached Sarvesh Kushare, who won a historic silver medal. Kushare credited Shankar's advice for his improved performance during the competition. Shankar's own medal hopes were dashed before the event truly began. He now aims to compete in the decathlon despite his knee issue.

title: Can India replace a satellite in days? Vikram-1 opens a bigger space question
content: India’s space programme has traditionally been driven almost entirely by Isro. Private companies manufactured components, supplied technology and supported missions, but orbital launches remained the domain of the state. Vikram-1 changed that equation. For the first time, an Indian private company has demonstrated the ability to develop and operate an orbital launch vehicle.

title: Kansas teacher dragged out in handcuffs after clapping at data center meeting
content: A Kansas physics teacher faced arrest after clapping during a city commission meeting. Lux Claridge was removed and charged with interference and disorderly conduct. He was later released from jail after posting bail. Claridge stated the arrest would not deter his future public participation. The city commission approved zoning changes for the data center project.

title: Cricket club under fire after 'Clicky Ponting' finger-click cheating claim goes viral
content: An amateur cricket match has sparked controversy over alleged umpire deception. A fielder reportedly clicked his fingers to simulate an edge off the bat. This incident has led to a formal investigation by the league officials. Other similar allegations have also surfaced against the same club. The league is now examining the dismissals for deliberate deception.

title: US man arrested for wiping phone during airport search; Android OS may trouble Europe travellers
content: A federal case in Atlanta questions privacy software use as criminal intent evidence. Prosecutors accuse Samuel Tunick of wiping his phone to prevent authorities from accessing its contents. GrapheneOS, a privacy-focused operating system, is central to the ongoing legal proceedings. Authorities in Europe also reportedly view GrapheneOS usage with suspicion. GrapheneOS developers state their software is legal and protects against unauthorized data extraction.

title: Rare Amazon turtle hatchling born without its species’ dark colours
content: A rare albino turtle hatchling emerged in Bolivia’s Manuripi Reserve.  This unusual sighting draws attention to conservation efforts for vulnerable species.  Conservationists are closely monitoring turtle reproduction and nesting sites.  Habitat loss and illegal trade pose significant threats to native turtles.  Continued monitoring and protection are vital for species survival.

title: Why this church made of 40,000 human bones matters to history
content: The Sedlec Ossuary, a fascinating site in the Czech Republic, showcases a macabre yet mesmerizing collection of human skeletons. Artfully crafted by a monk alongside a skilled woodcarver, the chapel’s story traces back to the 13th century when soil from Jerusalem was brought here. As the cemetery overflowed with victims of the plague and fallen Crusaders, this haunting space becomes a profound reflection on mortality and commemoration.

title: How Europe's heatwave is proving Americans right about air conditioning
content: Europeans are now buying air conditioning units in unprecedented numbers. This trend is driven by record heatwaves and rising health concerns across the continent. Manufacturers report significant sales growth for cooling solutions in several European countries. Previously, air conditioning was viewed as an unnecessary luxury by many Europeans. This cultural shift reflects a growing understanding of cooling as an essential need.

title: Maharashtra CM directs withdrawal of FIRs against protesters involved in NEET stir
content: Maharashtra's Chief Minister has ordered the withdrawal of cases against protesting students.  These cases were registered during recent demonstrations supporting the Cockroach Janta Party.  Opposition parties urged the government to formally withdraw these pending legal actions.  Advocates warned that these cases could jeopardize students' futures and career prospects.  The Home Department will issue the necessary orders for case withdrawal soon.

title: 'Milestone' vs 'Pradhan saved Pradhan Mantri': Centre, oppn clash over anti-paper leak bill
content: The Lok Sabha is discussing a proposed amendment to the anti-paper leak law. This legislation aims to strengthen safeguards against examination fraud following the NEET exam leak. Union minister Jitendra Singh introduced the bill, reaffirming government commitment to student welfare. Congress criticized the government's response and the handling of student protests. The opposition also questioned the prioritization of social media over education reforms.

title: How South African legend inspired Collins Saliboko’s Commonwealth dream
content: Tanzanian swimmer Collins Saliboko says Chad Le Clos's Commonwealth Games career, including a 19th medal won at Glasgow 2026 that made him the event's most decorated male athlete, has shaped his own belief that African swimmers can reach the podium. Saliboko, 24, competed in the 100m freestyle at Glasgow 2026 after making his Olympic debut at Paris 2024, and is next entered in the 200m freestyle.

title: How Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry are changing children’s lives
content: Stephen Curry and Ayesha Curry received the 2026 Muhammad Ali Sports Humanitarian Award for the lasting impact of their Eat. Learn. Play. Foundation in Oakland. Since 2019, the foundation has delivered 35 million meals, distributed more than one million books, invested over $20 million in literacy programs and transformed schools and play spaces for children. Their commitment also extended to a charity lunch with Warren Buffett that helped raise millions for nonprofits, showing how the Golden State Warriors star continues to create change far beyond basketball.

title: Who are Ilia Topuria’s parents? Their Georgian roots and career influence
content: Zaza and Inga helped UFC star Ilia Topuria rise from a Georgian refugee family to world MMA stardom. Their story takes place in Germany, Georgia and Spain, each move creating the environment in which Ilia and his brother Aleksandre grew up with their combat-sports dreams. Early wrestling would have been a professional fighting dream without their work sacrifices and support.

title: Roberto Mancini returns to rescue Italy after three straight FIFA World Cup misses
content: Roberto Mancini has been appointed Italy's new head coach, tasked with rebuilding the national team.  He previously led Italy to European Championship glory in 2021.  The team failed to qualify for the last three FIFA World Cups.  Claudio Ranieri joins as the federation's new technical director.  Mancini faces immediate challenges in the Nations League competition.

title: Ranbir Kapoor's 'Ramayana' trailer to release on July 30
content: The highly anticipated Ramayana: Part 1 trailer will premiere worldwide on July 30. This auspicious trailer launch is scheduled for Thursday at 4:15 AM IST. Fans expressed immense excitement across social media platforms following the official announcement. The film, directed by Nitesh Tiwari, features a star-studded ensemble cast. Ramayana: Part 1 is slated for a Diwali 2026 theatrical release.

title: Major changes in India support staff: Assistant coach quits; new fielding coach appointed
content: Ryan ten Doeschate has resigned as India's assistant coach after two years. Subhadeep Ghosh will now serve as the team's new fielding coach. Ten Doeschate cited personal reasons for stepping away from the demanding role. His final assignment was the recent white-ball tour of England. Ghosh's first international assignment will be the Sri Lanka Test series.

title: Gandhis vs Pralhad Joshi: 'Defender of rapists' charge meets 'authenticate it' challenge
content: Congress leaders Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and Rahul Gandhi criticised the Prime Minister's choice for education minister. They alleged the minister expressed happiness over the release of convicted rapists. This accusation stems from remarks made regarding the Bilkis Bano case convicts. The opposition leaders demanded substantiation of these serious allegations. The Union minister denied the claims and sought an apology from the Congress MP.

title: FIDE reveals host city for Gukesh vs Sindarov World Championship clash
content: Geneva, Switzerland, will host the 2026 FIDE World Championship Match.  Reigning champion Gukesh Dommaraju will defend his title against Javokhir Sindarov.  This historic contest will feature the youngest players ever to compete for the championship.  The match is scheduled to take place from November 25 to December 15.  FIDE selected Geneva as a neutral venue for this significant chess event.

title: Sana Saeed on battling bulimia for 6 years: 'I carried so much shame'
content: Actress Sana Saeed, best known for playing Shah Rukh Khan's daughter in 'Kuch Kuch Hota Hai', has opened up about her six-year battle with bulimia and the four years it took her to fully recover. In a new interview, the actress spoke about the shame she carried, the turning point in her healing, and the pressures around body image that shaped her struggle.

title: India’s 'looksmaxxing' economy: More science, more spending, fewer taboos
content: India's beauty market is rapidly expanding, driven by evolving consumer attitudes and increased awareness. Skincare routines now feature advanced ingredients, replacing older methods. Cosmetic procedures are becoming mainstream, with many seeking subtle enhancements. Digital platforms and influencers significantly shape purchasing decisions for beauty products. This shift reflects a move towards personalized wellness and a broader definition of beauty.

title: Govt must stop targeting, witch-hunting students: CJP warns of fresh peaceful protest
content: Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder, has warned of a fresh nationwide protest. This action will occur if police harassment of students continues. Dipke stated the Cockroach Janta Party will respond with a massive peaceful protest. The government must stop targeting and witch-hunting students. This warning was issued via a post on X on Tuesday.

title: 'They still have plenty to offer': 'Asian Bradman' backs Virat, Rohit for 2027 World Cup
content: Zaheer Abbas, the former Pakistan captain, has thrown his weight behind Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma for the upcoming 2027 ODI World Cup. He emphasises that their vast experience and skills are crucial for India’s success. Abbas argues that fitness and scoring abilities should outweigh any concerns about age. Rohit’s recent impressive century against England has particularly strengthened his support for both senior players.

title: Ravi Mohan divorce case: Court rejects Rs 40 lakh alimony plea
content: The Chennai Family Welfare Court rejected a Rs 40 lakh monthly alimony plea.  Ravi Mohan must now pay Rs 3 lakh monthly until divorce proceedings conclude.  The court also allowed the actor unrestricted meetings with his two sons.  This order addresses financial and visitation disputes in the ongoing divorce case.  The long-running legal battle between Ravi Mohan and Aarti continues.

title: Ex-India U-19 WC hero stays behind bars after bail denied in match-fixing case
content: Manjot Kalra remains in Sri Lankan custody after a court rejected his bail plea. Investigators are pursuing a high-profile corruption probe linked to the Lanka Premier League. Several Sri Lankan cricketers have lodged complaints regarding alleged match-fixing approaches. Authorities possess recorded evidence connecting to the alleged approaches made to players. The controversy has also led to the termination of the Jaffna Kings franchise ownership.

title: Global race for sixth‑gen fighters heats up as GCAP demonstrator to fly by 2027
content: The United Kingdom unveiled its combat air flying demonstrator aircraft. This aircraft will lead development for the sixth-generation Tempest fighter program.  Other nations are also advancing their own advanced fighter jet projects.  China is rapidly progressing with its stealth fighter development and prototypes.  India must accelerate its indigenous efforts or seek international partnerships.

title: Missile shortage forces US Army to return to older PAC-2 Patriot interceptors
content: The US Army has ordered Patriot PAC-2 GEM-T missiles after a thirty-year hiatus.  This move addresses critical missile shortages driven by global conflicts and demand.  Ukraine and several allied nations are also procuring these effective ballistic missile interceptors.  Raytheon and Lockheed Martin are increasing production of various Patriot missile variants.  These efforts aim to stabilize munitions supply chains for ongoing operational needs.

title: History made! West Indies pacer achieves never-seen-before feat vs Pak
content: Justin Greaves made Test cricket history with five consecutive wicket-maidens. He achieved this remarkable feat against Pakistan during the opening Test match. Greaves finished with career-best figures of five wickets for just twenty-seven runs. This performance triggered a dramatic collapse in the Pakistan batting lineup. The West Indies all-rounder secured a significant first-innings lead for his team.

title: 'Issue far from settled': Govt rejects Meta's explanation on 'removal' of PM Modi's video
content: The Centre finds Meta's explanation for Prime Minister Modi's post removal unsatisfactory. Government sources stated the issue requires deeper discussions with the social media company. Meta's response was deemed unreasonable by officials after the post was briefly unavailable. The ministry summoned Meta's global head of public policy regarding the incident. Discussions with Meta will continue as the matter is far from settled.

title: Delhi Police attempted to arrest Aishe Ghosh, alleges SFI
content: The SFI, the student wing of the Communist Party of India (Marxist) [CPI(M)], stated that its members resisted the arrest when the police barged into the party office at the AKG Bhavan

title: M.S. Swaminathan Research Foundation, civic bodies ink pact on solid waste management, public health project

content: The Shimla Agreement committed both countries to resolving their disputes, including Kashmir, through direct negotiation.
